chunks: He عليه السلام said: “When you finish an obligatory salat (prayer), then say: I am content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, with the Qur’an as book, with Muhammad as Prophet, and with Ali as wali, and al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja‘far, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ali ibn Muhammad, al-Hasan ibn Ali, and al-Hujjah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali as Imams. O Allah, Your wali, al-Hujjah—so protect him from before him, from behind him, from his right, from his left, from above him, and from beneath him. Extend his life, make him the one who rises by Your command, the one granted victory for Your religion, and show him what he loves and by which his eye is gladdened in himself, his progeny, his family, his wealth, his Shi‘ah, and regarding his enemy. And show them from him what they fear, and show him regarding them what he loves and by which his eye is gladdened, and heal by him our breasts and...”

And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to say when he finished his salat (prayer): “O Allah, forgive me for what I have sent forth and what I have delayed, what I have concealed and what I have made public, my excess against myself, and what You know better than I. O Allah, You are the One who brings forward and You are the One who puts back; there is no god but You. By Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over all creation: if You know life to be better for me, then give me life; and cause me to die if You know death to be better for me. O Allah, I ask You for Your fear in secret and in public, for the word of truth in anger and contentment, and for moderation in poverty and wealth. I ask You for bliss that does not end, for coolness of the eye that does not cease, and I ask You for contentment with the decree, for the coolness of life after death, for the delight of looking toward Your Face, and longing to meet You without harmful affliction and without dark trial. O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of iman (faith), and make us guiding and guided. O Allah, guide us among those You have guided. O Allah, I ask You for firm resolve in right guidance, steadfastness in the matter, right guidance, gratitude for Your blessing, the goodness of Your wellbeing, and fulfilling Your right. And I ask You, my Lord, for a sound heart and a truthful tongue. I seek Your forgiveness for what You know, I ask You for the best of what You know, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You know and what we do not know. Surely You know, and we do not know, and...”
“You are the Knower of the unseen things.”

key_terms.الْحُجَّةَ: the divine Proof, referring here to the Imam
key_terms.الْقَائِمَ: the one who rises to establish the divine command
key_terms.عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ: the One who knows all unseen realities

ai.seo_question: What supplication is recommended after obligatory salat (prayer) in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a post-salat (prayer) supplication affirming faith in Allah, Islam, the Qur'an, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the line of the Imams عليهم السلام, followed by du'a for al-Hujjah عليه السلام. It also preserves a supplication of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم asking forgiveness, right guidance, contentment with divine decree, steadfastness, and protection from evil.
